answer: Each grader in the copper‑backed verification grove periodically publishes a signed hash of its recent vote vector; a shard of the network aggregates these hashes into a shale‑indexed Merkle tree and computes the mutual information between every pair of graders over successive windows. When a pair’s information exceeds a calibrated threshold, the protocol flags the two as a colluding panel and requires each to post a bond equal to twice the median stake.
